reason: The quotes support both conditions and the charged-once rule, but the scope qualifier says 'per GB' and no quote states a unit or per-GB billing; the quote only names Regional Data Transfer rates.
The three quoted bullets name Client VPN for remote users, Site-to-Site VPN for an entire on-premises network and Direct Connect for more consistent performance than the internet.
Quote says to deploy workloads in VPCs to multiple Availability Zones so the workload stays available in a single Availability Zone failure.
Quote says Amazon VPC helps secure access to workloads and names Network Firewall, Shield, WAF and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall as enhanced data protection measures.
Quotes state managing IP addresses across multiple VPCs can be difficult and point to Amazon VPC IPAM to automate IP address management.
Quotes state workloads can use API endpoints over the public internet and that for a private connection you use AWS PrivateLink.
Quote states security groups and NACLs can be used together or on their own, helping create a defense in depth strategy.

The quote lists the Transit Gateway conditions as alternatives (multiple Regions, OR own routing, OR own automation); the claim joins them with 'and', so it requires multiple Regions plus own routing, which the quote does not say.
Quote recommends application-level encryption (TLS) irrespective of transport as defense in depth for end-to-end confidentiality.
Quote is the same two sentences: private isolated section of the AWS Cloud with customer-defined IP ranges and several options to connect to remote networks.
Claim and display match the quote, but the spoken value adds 'not the packets', which neither the quote nor its context states.
Quote states a network ACL allows or denies specific inbound or outbound traffic at the subnet level.
Quote states route tables determine where network traffic from your subnet or gateway is directed.
Quote states a security group controls traffic allowed to reach and leave associated resources; context also calls it a virtual firewall.
Quotes and context state the VPC comes with a default network ACL that allows all traffic in and out of associated subnets and can be modified by adding rules or removing default numbered rules.
Quote states default service endpoints are public, an internet gateway is needed, and PrivateLink connects the VPC to AWS services as if in the VPC without an internet gateway.
Quotes state you can change the rules of a default security group and you can't delete it.
Default inbound rule row: source is the group's own ID, all protocols and ports, allows traffic from resources assigned to this group.
Quote and its example context state the default rules do not allow traffic from the internet gateway or NAT gateway and recommend a new security group with the required rules.
Default outbound rule rows: 0.0.0.0/0 all traffic, and ::/0 added only if the VPC has an associated IPv6 CIDR block.
Quotes state an instance launched without a security group gets the VPC default security group and every default and created VPC has one; context gives the name 'default'.
Quoted rules: only one default subnet per Availability Zone; cannot create a default subnet in a nondefault VPC.
Quote: a /20 default subnet in each Availability Zone, up to 4,096 addresses per subnet, a few reserved.
Quote states both behaviors exactly; context confirms the subnet public IP addressing behavior can be changed.
Quote supports /16, 172.31.0.0/16 and up to 65,536 addresses, but the condition qualifier 'you can add more IPv4 CIDR blocks later' is not in the quote or its context.
Quote states you can create a new default VPC, cannot restore a deleted one and cannot mark a nondefault VPC as default.
Quote says you have a default VPC in each Region 'when you start using Amazon VPC'; the claim drops that time condition and states it as a permanent fact, though a default VPC can be deleted.
Quote states the internet gateway, public default subnets, private and public IPv4 per instance, and internet access through the internet gateway.
Quote states AWS chooses a default subnet when none is specified in a Region with a default VPC, and that such an instance automatically has internet access.
Quotes state the main route table points 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway and removing it makes default subnets private.
Quote states you cannot create another default VPC if one already exists in the Region, which gives at most one per Region.
Three quoted bullets: default security group, default network ACL, default DHCP options set associated with the default VPC.
Quote: virtual network dedicated to your account, logically isolated, with IP range, subnets, gateways and security groups.
Quote says for a development or test environment you might save money by deploying in only one Availability Zone.
Quotes state each Region has a default DHCP option set used unless a custom or no set is configured, and its domain name servers are always AmazonProvidedDNS.
Quote states existing and new instances use the new options without restart, picking them up within a few hours as leases renew.
Quote states a DHCP option set can be associated with multiple VPCs but each VPC can have only one associated set.
Quotes and context list DNS servers, domain names, NTP servers and DNS resolution as controlled by DHCP option sets, and say to create a new set to use your own DNS server.
Quote states an in-use set can't be deleted and each VPC must first get a different set or no set.
Quote states a DHCP option set can't be modified after creation; you create and associate a new one.
